title: Kick Trump Off the Ballot? Even Liberal Justices Are Skeptical

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Benjamin Poulin，我是Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，展示着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》节目。

sentences.en: We are following breaking news.
sentences.zh: 我们正在关注突发新闻。

sentences.en: The Colorado Supreme Court has ruled that former President Donald Trump will be left off the state's primary and presidential ballots.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州最高法院裁定，前总统唐纳德·特朗普将不得出现在该州的初选和总统大选选票上。

sentences.en: In December, the Colorado Supreme Court issued a bombshell ruling.
sentences.zh: 去年12月，科罗拉多州最高法院发布了一项重磅裁决。

sentences.en: This is a historic decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个历史性的决定。

sentences.en: It's a momentous decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个意义重大的决定。

sentences.en: That said Donald Trump was ineligible to be on the state's ballot for the Republican presidential primary.
sentences.zh: 裁决称，唐纳德·特朗普没有资格出现在该州的共和党总统初选选票上。

sentences.en: Because of his alleged role in the January 6th insurrection.
sentences.zh: 原因是他涉嫌在1月6日的骚乱中扮演了角色。

sentences.en: Because, it found, he had engaged in insurrection on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 因为法院认定，他在1月6日参与了叛乱。

sentences.en: It's based on a little-known provision that bars people who have engaged in an insurrection from holding government office.
sentences.zh: 这是基于一条鲜为人知的条款，该条款禁止参与叛乱的人担任政府公职。

sentences.en: Which, according to the 14th Amendment, disqualifies him from serving as president.
sentences.zh: 根据第14修正案，这剥夺了他担任总统的资格。

sentences.en: It states that anyone engaging in insurrection cannot hold public office.
sentences.zh: 该条款规定，任何参与叛乱的人都不得担任公职。

sentences.en: But this is unprecedented constitutional territory, y'all.
sentences.zh: 但各位，这可是前所未有的宪法领域。

sentences.en: The Civil War-era constitutional provision could knock the leading candidate of one of the two major political parties off the ballot.
sentences.zh: 这条内战时期的宪法条款，可能会将两大政党之一的主要候选人踢出选票。

sentences.en: At the time, we turned to our colleague, Adam Liptak, who covers the Supreme Court for The Times, to help us understand the meaning of that decision and what could happen next.
sentences.zh: 当时，我们求助于负责《纽约时报》最高法院报道的同事Adam Liptak，请他帮我们解读这一裁决的含义以及接下来可能发生的情况。

sentences.en: This really needs to be an issue that is resolved on a nationwide basis, meaning it has to go to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这确实需要作为一个在全国范围内解决的问题，也就是说，它必须上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: And it would be shocking if the Supreme Court would not wade in and issue a ruling on this question that, you know, a decade ago would have been impossible to imagine.
sentences.zh: 如果最高法院不介入并就这个问题做出裁决，那才令人震惊，要知道，这在十年前是无法想象的。

sentences.en: Just as Adam predicted, the Supreme Court did take the case.
sentences.zh: 正如Adam所预料的那样，最高法院确实受理了此案。

sentences.en: It's Friday.
sentences.zh: 今天是周五。

sentences.en: February 9th.
sentences.zh: 2月9日。

sentences.en: Adam, I really like your—what do the kids call it?
sentences.zh: Adam，我很喜欢你的——现在的年轻人管这叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Your fit?
sentences.zh: 你的穿搭（fit）？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I like your shirt.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你的衬衫。

sentences.en: It's a very handsome, business-casual kind of thing going on there.
sentences.zh: 看起来非常帅气，是一种商务休闲风。

sentences.en: It's barely business, but it is casual.
sentences.zh: 算不上商务，但确实挺休闲的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Adam, the clock strikes 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 那么，Adam，时钟敲响了上午10点，

sentences.en: or so this morning, Thursday, and the Supreme Court begins to hear this momentous case.
sentences.zh: 也就是今天周四上午，最高法院开始审理这起重大案件。

sentences.en: Take us into the room.
sentences.zh: 带我们进入现场吧。

sentences.en: So, this is the biggest election case since at least Bush v.
sentences.zh: 这是自至少“布什诉戈尔案”以来最大的选举案件，

sentences.en: Gore, the 2000 decision that handed the presidency to George W.
sentences.zh: 那是在2000年，该裁决将总统职位判给了乔治·W·布什。

sentences.en: Bush.
sentences.zh: 布什。

sentences.en: And now the question is whether Donald Trump is eligible to be on the ballot in Colorado, but really all across the nation, under a provision of the Constitution that says,
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，根据宪法中的一条条款，唐纳德·特朗普是否有资格出现在科罗拉多州，乃至全国各地的选票上，该条款规定：

sentences.en: if you've sworn an oath to support the Constitution and then engage in insurrection, you may not hold any office.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾宣誓支持宪法，随后又参与了叛乱，你就不得担任任何公职。

sentences.en: The court had put the case on an exceptionally fast track, partly because ballots in Colorado are going out in a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 法院将此案列入了极速审理程序，部分原因是科罗拉多州的选票几天内就要发出去了。

sentences.en: Super Tuesday is almost upon us, and the nation needs an answer to whether the leading candidate of one of the political parties is even eligible to hold office.
sentences.zh: “超级星期二”即将到来，全国需要一个答案：其中一个政党的主要候选人是否还有资格担任公职。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Colorado, of course, is one of the Super Tuesday states that's going to be holding a Republican primary on March 5th.
sentences.zh: 当然，科罗拉多州是将在3月5日举行共和党初选的“超级星期二”州之一。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, the courtroom, of course, just across the street from the Capitol, where in January 6th, 2021, there was the cataclysmic assault on the seat of our government.
sentences.zh: 那么，法庭就在国会大厦街对面，2021年1月6日，那里发生了针对我们政府核心的灾难性袭击。

sentences.en: And you might think that that would have occupied a substantial part of the argument.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为这会占据辩论的很大一部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Given what this case is about.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这个案件的主题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That question of, was it an insurrection?
sentences.zh: 关于“这是否是一场叛乱”的问题，

sentences.en: Did Donald Trump, in sight, engage in that insurrection?
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普是否煽动并参与了那场叛乱？

sentences.en: And although those topics were not wholly absent from the argument, they came up in passing a couple times, that really was not the focus of the argument.
sentences.zh: 虽然这些话题在辩论中并非完全没有提及，也曾被顺带提过几次，但这确实不是辩论的焦点。

sentences.en: This was a legal argument about how the constitutional provision in this case works.
sentences.zh: 这是一场关于本案中宪法条款如何运作的法律辩论。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's then talk about the arguments made around that.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来谈谈围绕这一点提出的论点。

sentences.en: We'll hear argument this morning in case 23-7-19, Trump versus Anderson.
sentences.zh: 今天上午我们将审理23-7-19号案件，特朗普诉安德森案。

sentences.en: Mr. Mitchell?
sentences.zh: Mitchell先生？

sentences.en: So, there are two basic arguments in the case.
sentences.zh: 此案有两个基本论点。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官，法官阁下。

sentences.en: Jonathan Mitchell, Trump's lawyer, stands up.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的律师Jonathan Mitchell站了起来。

sentences.en: The Colorado Supreme Court's decision is wrong and should be reversed for numerous independent reasons.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州最高法院的裁决是错误的，应基于多个独立理由予以推翻。

sentences.en: He starts off with his lead argument,
sentences.zh: 他首先提出了他的核心论点，

sentences.en: which is a very close reading of Section 3 of the 14th Amendment that the Colorado Supreme Court used to say that Trump is not eligible to be president again.
sentences.zh: 即对第14修正案第3条的严谨解读，科罗拉多州最高法院正是利用该条款认定特朗普不再有资格担任总统。

sentences.en: The first reason is that President Trump is not covered by Section 3 because the president is not an officer of the United States, as that term is used,
sentences.zh: 第一个理由是，特朗普总统不受第3条的约束，因为总统不是宪法中所称的“合众国官员”，

sentences.en: throughout the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 宪法通篇都是这样使用该术语的。

sentences.en: It probably helps, Michael, to parse through the words.
sentences.zh: Michael，解析一下这些措辞可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: And there are three different ideas embedded in the amendment.
sentences.zh: 修正案中包含了三个不同的概念。

sentences.en: There's, first of all, who does it apply to?
sentences.zh: 首先，它适用于谁？

sentences.en: And it says you have to have previously taken an oath as a member of Congress or as an officer of the United States or as a member of any state legislature or as an executive or judicial officer of any state.
sentences.zh: 它说你必须曾以国会议员、合众国官员、州议会议员或州行政或司法官员的身份宣誓。

sentences.en: An officer of the United States refers only to appointed officials, and it does not encompass elected individuals such as the president or members of Congress.
sentences.zh: “合众国官员”仅指被任命的官员，不包括总统或国会议员等民选个人。

sentences.en: And he argues that you can't fit the president into the phrase, an officer of the United States, that those are appointed, not elected officials.
sentences.zh: 他认为你不能把总统归入“合众国官员”这一短语中，因为那是被任命的，而非民选的官员。

sentences.en: So that's his first textual argument about who it applies to.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他关于适用对象的第一个文本论点。

sentences.en: Second textual argument, what offices does it apply to?
sentences.zh: 第二个文本论点是，它适用于哪些职位？

sentences.en: And here I'm going to read a different part of the section.
sentences.zh: 这里我要读一下该条款的另一部分。

sentences.en: It says no person shall be a senator or representative in Congress or elector of president and vice president or hold any office, civil or military, under the United States.
sentences.zh: 它说：任何人不得担任国会议员、总统和副总统选举人，或担任合众国属下的任何文职或军职。

sentences.en: You'll notice the president is not mentioned by name, although he would seem to hold an office, civil or military.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到总统没有被点名，尽管他似乎确实担任着文职或军职。

sentences.en: But there are arguments, again, that it doesn't apply.
sentences.zh: 但同样有论点认为它不适用。

sentences.en: And then there's the phrase, hold any office.
sentences.zh: 还有“担任任何公职”这一短语。

sentences.en: And Mitchell says, Because even if the candidate is an admitted insurrectionist, Section 3 still allows the candidate to run for office and even win election to office.
sentences.zh: Mitchell说，因为即使候选人是公认的叛乱分子，第3条仍然允许该候选人竞选公职，甚至赢得选举。

sentences.en: You can't hold an office, but it doesn't say you can't run for office.
sentences.zh: 你不能担任公职，但它没说你不能竞选公职。

sentences.en: It doesn't say you can't be elected to office.
sentences.zh: 它没说你不能当选公职。

sentences.en: So if a state banned even an admitted insurrectionist from the ballot, it would be adding to and altering the Constitution's qualifications for office.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个州禁止哪怕是公认的叛乱分子出现在选票上，那将是在增加和改变宪法规定的任职资格。

sentences.en: Because under Section 3...
sentences.zh: 因为根据第3条……

sentences.en: And he takes some additional comfort from the last clause of Section 3.
sentences.zh: 他从第3条的最后条款中得到了一些额外的安慰。

sentences.en: Section 3 cannot be used to exclude a presidential candidate from the ballot, even if that candidate is disqualified from serving as president under Section 3.
sentences.zh: 第3条不能用于将总统候选人排除在选票之外，即使该候选人根据第3条被取消了担任总统的资格。

sentences.en: Because Congress can lift that disability after the candidate is elected, but before he takes office.
sentences.zh: 因为国会可以在候选人当选后、就职前取消这种限制。

sentences.en: So he says, even someone who is disqualified can run, can be elected, because the moment before Inauguration Day, Congress can say, by a two-thirds vote of each house,
sentences.zh: 所以他说，即使是被取消资格的人也可以参选，可以当选，因为在就职典礼前的那一刻，国会可以通过两院三分之二的投票，

sentences.en: that the person is eligible after all.
sentences.zh: 宣布此人其实是有资格的。

sentences.en: So it's not lawful to bar someone from the candidacy when, at least in theory, Congress can make you eligible right up to the point of inauguration.
sentences.zh: 因此，禁止某人参选是不合法的，因为至少在理论上，国会可以在就职典礼前的最后一刻让你获得资格。

sentences.en: And in this situation, a ruling from this court that affirms the decision below would not only violate term limits,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，法院维持下级法院裁决的判决不仅会违反任期限制，

sentences.en: but take away the votes of potentially tens of millions of Americans.
sentences.zh: 还会剥夺数千万美国人的选票。

sentences.en: I welcome the court's questions.
sentences.zh: 欢迎法官提问。

sentences.en: OK, so this admittedly is very technical, but there are three things going on here, right?
sentences.zh: 好的，这确实非常专业，但这里有三件事，对吧？

sentences.en: First, Trump's lawyer is saying that this doesn't apply to presidents or former presidents because they're not mentioned specifically in this rule.
sentences.zh: 首先，特朗普的律师说，这不适用于总统或前总统，因为这条规则中没有明确提到他们。

sentences.en: Secondly, he's saying it doesn't prevent anyone from seeking the office of the presidency because that office isn't specifically mentioned in this rule.
sentences.zh: 其次，他说这并不阻止任何人寻求总统职位，因为该职位没有在这条规则中明确提及。

sentences.en: And finally, it doesn't say anything about barring people from running for office.
sentences.zh: 最后，它没有提到禁止人们竞选公职。

sentences.en: It only bars people from holding certain offices.
sentences.zh: 它只是禁止人们担任某些公职。

sentences.en: So for all of those reasons, Trump's lawyer is saying this doesn't apply to Trump and that the Colorado Supreme Court, in its finding, has been wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以基于所有这些原因，特朗普的律师说这不适用于特朗普，科罗拉多州最高法院的裁定是错误的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Mr. Murray?
sentences.zh: Murray先生？

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官，法官阁下。

sentences.en: Jason Murray, the lawyer for the six Colorado voters challenging Trump's eligibility, says all of that is wrong.
sentences.zh: 挑战特朗普参选资格的六名科罗拉多州选民的律师Jason Murray表示，这一切都是错误的。

sentences.en: He says Section 3 disqualifies all oath-breaking insurrectionists except a former president who never before held other state or federal office.
sentences.zh: 他说，第3条取消了所有违背誓言的叛乱分子的资格，除了从未担任过其他州或联邦公职的前总统。

sentences.en: There is no possible rationale for such an exemption.
sentences.zh: 这种豁免没有任何合理的依据。

sentences.en: That it would be an insane way to interpret the constitutional provision to exclude the most important office in the land and the highest executive official of the United States from a provision meant to safeguard democracy from insurrection.
sentences.zh: 如果将国家最重要的职位和最高行政官员排除在旨在保护民主免受叛乱影响的条款之外，那将是一种疯狂的宪法解释方式。

sentences.en: Section 3 uses deliberately broad language to cover all positions of federal power requiring an oath to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 第3条使用了刻意宽泛的语言，涵盖了所有需要向宪法宣誓的联邦权力职位。

sentences.en: He also makes the point that Section 3 is similar to other kinds of qualifications to be president.
sentences.zh: 他还指出，第3条类似于其他类型的总统任职资格。

sentences.en: States are allowed to safeguard their ballots by excluding those who are underage, foreign-born.
sentences.zh: 各州被允许通过排除未成年人、非出生于本国的人来保护其选票。

sentences.en: You have to be 35 years old.
sentences.zh: 你必须年满35岁。

sentences.en: You have to be a natural-born citizen of the United States.
sentences.zh: 你必须是合众国的出生公民。

sentences.en: He's saying, use your common sense, justices.
sentences.zh: 他是在说，法官们，用用你们的常识吧。

sentences.en: This does apply to the president.
sentences.zh: 这确实适用于总统。

sentences.en: That's pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 这一点很清楚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Under Article 2 and the 10th Amendment,
sentences.zh: 根据第2条和第10修正案，

sentences.en: states have the power to ensure that their citizens' electoral votes are not wasted on a candidate who is constitutionally barred from holding office.
sentences.zh: 各州有权确保其公民的选举人票不会浪费在宪法禁止担任公职的候选人身上。

sentences.en: He says it's a crazy way to run a system that people can vote for Donald Trump and not know whether their vote is going to count,
sentences.zh: 他说，如果人们投票给唐纳德·特朗普，却不知道他们的选票是否有效，这是一种疯狂的制度运作方式，

sentences.en: depending on whether his current disqualification from running for office is perhaps lifted by Congress, and not only by Congress, by a two-thirds vote of each house,
sentences.zh: 这取决于他目前被禁止竞选公职的资格是否可能被国会取消，而且不仅仅是由国会，而是由两院三分之二的投票取消，

sentences.en: which is a little hard to imagine.
sentences.zh: 这有点难以想象。

sentences.en: We are here because for the first time since the war of 1812, our nation's capital came under violent assault.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以在这里，是因为自1812年战争以来，我们的国家首都第一次遭到暴力袭击。

sentences.en: For the first time in history, the attack was incited by a sitting president of the United States to disrupt the peaceful transfer of presidential power.
sentences.zh: 历史上第一次，这次袭击是由一位在任的美国总统煽动的，目的是破坏总统权力的和平移交。

sentences.en: I welcome the court's questions.
sentences.zh: 欢迎法官提问。

sentences.en: And how do the justices, Adam, respond to these two clashing claims of this close reading of the 14th Amendment by a lawyer for Trump and a lawyer for the Colorado voters?
sentences.zh: Adam，法官们是如何回应特朗普律师和科罗拉多州选民律师对第14修正案的这种截然不同的解读的？

sentences.en: So, at first, it seems like the justices are going to divide along predictable lines,
sentences.zh: 起初，法官们似乎会沿着可预测的路线分裂，

sentences.en: with conservative justices like Neil Gorsuch and Samuel Alito being open to this kind of close textual reading.
sentences.zh: 像Neil Gorsuch和Samuel Alito这样的保守派法官对这种严谨的文本解读持开放态度。

sentences.en: Mr. Mitchell, stepping back on this, a lot hinges on the difference between, in your argument, between the term office and officer.
sentences.zh: Mitchell先生，退一步讲，在你的论点中，很多东西取决于“职位”（office）和“官员”（officer）这两个词之间的区别。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm wondering, what theory do you have, from an original understanding or a textualist perspective,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，从原始理解或文本主义的角度来看，你有什么理论，

sentences.en: why those two terms so closely related would carry such different weight?
sentences.zh: 为什么这两个如此紧密相关的术语会有如此不同的权重？

sentences.en: And some of the liberals seem skeptical of Trump's lawyer's argument.
sentences.zh: 而一些自由派法官似乎对特朗普律师的论点持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Justice Kagan?
sentences.zh: Kagan大法官？

sentences.en: Justice Kagan, for instance, kind of throws up her hands, saying, You know, if they had thought about it, what reason would they have given for that rule?
sentences.zh: 例如，Kagan大法官摊了摊手，说：“你知道，如果他们考虑过这个问题，他们会给出什么理由来制定那条规则呢？”

sentences.en: And it does seem as though there's no particular reason, and you can think of lots of reasons for the contrary,
sentences.zh: 而且似乎确实没有任何特别的理由，你反而可以想到很多反面的理由，

sentences.en: to say that the only people who have engaged in insurrection who are not disqualified from office are presidents who have not held high office before.
sentences.zh: 去说唯一没有被取消公职资格的叛乱分子，就是那些之前没有担任过高级公职的总统。

sentences.en: Why would that rule exist?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有这样的规则？

sentences.en: Let's be serious here.
sentences.zh: 让我们严肃点。

sentences.en: It can't be that the president is not included in these catch-all, all-encompassing phrases on something so important.
sentences.zh: 总统不可能不被包含在这些如此重要的、包罗万象的短语中。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And is there any better reason for saying that an insurrectionist cannot hold the whole panoply of offices in the United States,
sentences.zh: 有什么更好的理由说叛乱分子不能担任美国所有的公职，

sentences.en: but we're perfectly fine with that insurrectionist being president?
sentences.zh: 但我们却完全可以接受那个叛乱分子担任总统？

sentences.en: I think that's an even tougher argument for us to make.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对我们来说是一个更难辩护的论点。

sentences.en: Justice Sotomayor?
sentences.zh: Sotomayor大法官？

sentences.en: I just want to pin down your principal argument on Section 3.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确定你关于第3条的主要论点。

sentences.en: And Justice Sonia Sotomayor, another liberal, makes the interesting point.
sentences.zh: 另一位自由派法官Sonia Sotomayor提出了一个有趣的观点。

sentences.en: Your principal argument is that the president is not an officer of the United States, correct?
sentences.zh: 你的主要论点是总统不是“合众国官员”，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say it a little more forcefully than what Your Honor just described.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会比阁下刚才描述的表达得更强硬一些。

sentences.en: A bit of a gerrymandered rule, isn't it, designed to benefit only your client?
sentences.zh: 这是一个有点“杰利蝾螈”（不公正划分）式的规则，不是吗？专门为了让你当事人受益？

sentences.en: That this argument seems to be, as she put it, gerrymandered to favor Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 正如她所说，这个论点似乎是为了偏袒唐纳德·特朗普而“量身定制”的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I certainly wouldn't call it gerrymandered.
sentences.zh: 我当然不会称之为“杰利蝾螈”。

sentences.en: That implies nefarious.
sentences.zh: 那意味着邪恶。

sentences.en: Well, you didn't make it up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你并不是凭空捏造的。

sentences.en: You remember that list of offices we discussed?
sentences.zh: 你还记得我们讨论过的那份职位清单吗？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 记得。

sentences.en: Every other president falls into one of the named offices.
sentences.zh: 其他每一位总统都属于其中提到的职位之一。

sentences.en: Joe Biden was a senator.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登曾是参议员。

sentences.en: Bill Clinton was a governor.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿曾是州长。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Donald Trump, though, didn't serve in any previous official government capacity.
sentences.zh: 然而，唐纳德·特朗普此前并未担任过任何政府公职。

sentences.en: He was a businessman, and then he became president.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名商人，后来成为了总统。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Virtually every other president except Washington has taken an oath to support the Constitution, correct?
sentences.zh: 除了华盛顿之外，几乎每一位总统都宣誓支持宪法，对吧？

sentences.en: And with the possible exception of George Washington, every other president fits into one of those other slots.
sentences.zh: 除了乔治·华盛顿这个可能的例外，其他每一位总统都符合那些职位中的一个。

sentences.en: So we have an argument here that's kind of a ticket for one ride only.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这里有一个论点，就像是一张单程票。

sentences.en: Applies only to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 仅适用于唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Sotomayor's point is that's a little too cute by half that you're coming up with an argument that applies to only one of our many presidents.
sentences.zh: 索托马约尔大法官的观点是，你提出的这个论点只适用于我们众多总统中的一位，这显得有点过于投机取巧了。

sentences.en: Or perhaps two, but the first one being the first when there really wasn't much of a precedent to think about.
sentences.zh: 或者也许是两位，但第一位是开国总统，当时并没有太多先例可供参考。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That gives you a sense of how technical, historical, originalist, that part of the argument was.
sentences.zh: 这让你了解了那部分论点在技术、历史和原旨主义层面上有多么深奥。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Justice Jackson?
sentences.zh: 杰克逊大法官？

sentences.en: I'm going back to whether the presidency is one of the barred offices.
sentences.zh: 我回到总统职位是否属于被禁止的职位这一问题上。

sentences.en: And then, in a little bit of a surprise, it turns out that not everyone is so predictable.
sentences.zh: 然后，令人有点惊讶的是，事实证明并非每个人都那么容易预测。

sentences.en: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, the third liberal, says it might actually make sense to her to exclude the presidency from Section 3.
sentences.zh: 第三位自由派大法官凯坦吉·布朗·杰克逊表示，将总统职位排除在第3条之外对她来说可能确实说得通。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: I didn't see any evidence that the presidency was top of mind for the framers when they were drafting Section 3 because they were actually dealing with a different issue.
sentences.zh: 我没有看到任何证据表明，起草第3条时，制宪者们首要考虑的是总统职位，因为他们当时实际上是在处理一个不同的问题。

sentences.en: The pressing concern, at least as I see the historical record, was actually what was going on at lower levels of the government.
sentences.zh: 据我所见的历史记录，当时紧迫的担忧实际上是政府低层正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: She says the people who adopted it were concerned with the possibility of insurrectionists infiltrating state government and that former Confederates would return to power in the South.
sentences.zh: 她说，采纳这一条款的人们担心叛乱分子渗透到州政府，以及前南方邦联成员会重掌南方大权。

sentences.en: But not that the national office, the president elected by the entire nation, would conceivably be a former Confederate.
sentences.zh: 但并不是担心国家层面的职位，即由全国选出的总统，可能会是前南方邦联成员。

sentences.en: And that's a very different lens.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常不同的视角。

sentences.en: She held herself out to be an originalist, and many people, particularly on the right, scoffed.
sentences.zh: 她自诩为原旨主义者，许多人，尤其是右翼人士，对此嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: But she has, in her brief tenure on the court, occasionally shown strong originalist impulses.
sentences.zh: 但在她任职法院的短暂期间，她偶尔表现出了强烈的原旨主义倾向。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And somewhat unexpectedly, that seems to be leading her to bolster an argument from Trump's lawyer here on whether or not this amendment really does apply to Trump.
sentences.zh: 出人意料的是，这似乎促使她支持特朗普律师的论点，即该修正案是否真的适用于特朗普。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: ...specifically mentioned the presidency and the vice presidency as an author.
sentences.zh: ……明确提到了总统和副总统作为作者。

sentences.en: But it wasn't the final enactment.
sentences.zh: 但那不是最终的法案。

sentences.en: It wasn't the final, it wasn't, yes, I'm sorry, it wasn't the final enactment,
sentences.zh: 那不是最终的，那不是，是的，抱歉，那不是最终的法案，

sentences.en: but it does show that there was some concern by some people about Confederate insurrectionists ascending to the presidency.
sentences.zh: 但这确实表明，有些人对南方邦联叛乱分子登上总统宝座感到担忧。

sentences.en: So, in listening to arguments on this first point, the main point pressed by Donald Trump's lawyers,
sentences.zh: 所以，在听取关于第一点的辩论时，也就是唐纳德·特朗普的律师们强调的主要观点，

sentences.en: it seemed like there was the beginning of the possibility of a scrambled lineup.
sentences.zh: 似乎出现了一种阵营混乱的可能性。

sentences.en: And as other issues were discussed in the case, that possibility seemed only to grow.
sentences.zh: 随着案件中讨论的其他问题，这种可能性似乎只增不减。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天使用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，在 nytimes.com/subscribe 获取特别优惠。

sentences.en: So, Adam, right before the break, we covered the first issue in this hearing, and the justices' responses were ideologically confusing.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，在休息之前，我们讨论了这次听证会的第一个问题，大法官们的反应在意识形态上令人困惑。

sentences.en: As you said, what happens with the second big issue in this hearing?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这次听证会的第二个大问题会发生什么？

sentences.en: The second question is whether individual states are entitled to disqualify presidential candidates.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是各州是否有权取消总统候选人的资格。

sentences.en: A state cannot exclude any candidate for federal office from the ballot on account of Section 3.
sentences.zh: 各州不得因第3条而将任何联邦公职候选人排除在选票之外。

sentences.en: Jonathan Mitchell, Trump's lawyer, presses this point also.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的律师乔纳森·米切尔也强调了这一点。

sentences.en: Unless and until Congress enacts implementing legislation allowing it to do so.
sentences.zh: 除非且直到国会颁布允许这样做的实施立法。

sentences.en: And says, Congress has to act, and we can't have one state here and one state there disqualifying candidates.
sentences.zh: 并表示，国会必须采取行动，我们不能让这个州或那个州随意取消候选人资格。

sentences.en: Only Congress can provide the means of enforcing Section 3.
sentences.zh: 只有国会才能提供执行第3条的手段。

sentences.en: Well, what would such congressional action look like?
sentences.zh: 那么，这样的国会行动会是什么样子？

sentences.en: What is he referring to?
sentences.zh: 他指的是什么？

sentences.en: You could imagine Congress enacting a law, saying here's what rights states do and don't have in making these determinations.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象国会颁布一项法律，说明各州在做出这些决定时拥有哪些权利，以及没有哪些权利。

sentences.en: It's just setting some ground rules.
sentences.zh: 这只是设定一些基本规则。

sentences.en: But then...
sentences.zh: 但是随后……

sentences.en: President Trump's other arguments for reversal ignore the constitutional role of the states.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统提出的其他推翻判决的论点忽略了宪法赋予各州的角色。

sentences.en: Jason Murray, the lawyer for the Colorado voters, says that's backwards.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州选民的律师杰森·默里表示，那是本末倒置。

sentences.en: States are allowed to safeguard their ballots by excluding those who are underage, foreign-born, running for a third presidential term,
sentences.zh: 各州被允许通过排除那些未成年、外国出生、竞选第三任总统任期的人来保护他们的选票，

sentences.en: or, as here, those who have engaged in insurrection against the Constitution in violation of their oath.
sentences.zh: 或者像这里的情况一样，排除那些违反誓言、参与针对宪法的叛乱的人。

sentences.en: That the Constitution assigns states the substantial role of conducting federal elections.
sentences.zh: 宪法赋予各州进行联邦选举的重要职责。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: And this is part of that role.
sentences.zh: 而这正是该职责的一部分。

sentences.en: It is kind of common knowledge, and we especially learned it in 2020, when President Trump tried to overturn the election results at the state level,
sentences.zh: 这几乎是常识，我们特别是在2020年学到了这一点，当时特朗普总统试图在州一级推翻选举结果，

sentences.en: that states very much are responsible for elections in this country, even federal elections, even the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 即各州确实对这个国家的选举负责，甚至是联邦选举，甚至是总统选举。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Okay, so what do the justices think about both of these arguments being made about whether a state like Colorado can try to knock someone like Trump off the ballot?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么大法官们对这两个关于科罗拉多州这样的州是否可以试图将特朗普踢出选票的论点有何看法？

sentences.en: The justices are very wary of giving this power in this context to individual states.
sentences.zh: 大法官们非常警惕在这种背景下将这种权力交给各个州。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole point of the 14th Amendment was to restrict state power, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，第14修正案的全部意义在于限制州权力，对吧？

sentences.en: Chief Justice Roberts says the whole point of the 14th Amendment, after all, adopted after the Civil War, adopted after states seceded from the Union,
sentences.zh: 首席大法官罗伯茨说，第14修正案毕竟是在内战后通过的，是在各州脱离联邦后通过的，

sentences.en: was to restrict state power, to augment federal power.
sentences.zh: 其全部意义在于限制州权力，增强联邦权力。

sentences.en: So wouldn't that be the last place that you'd look for authorization for the states, including Confederate states, to enforce the presidential election process?
sentences.zh: 那么，这难道不是你寻找授权各州（包括南方邦联州）执行总统选举程序的最后一个地方吗？

sentences.en: He's saying the 14th Amendment is at odds with the very idea of giving states such a power.
sentences.zh: 他是在说，第14修正案与赋予各州这种权力的想法本身就是相矛盾的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: No, Your Honor.
sentences.zh: 不，法官阁下。

sentences.en: First, we would locate the state's authority to run presidential elections, not in the 14th Amendment, but in Article 2.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们将州管理总统选举的权力定位在宪法第二条，而不是第14修正案中。

sentences.en: So Jason Murray, the lawyer for the Challengers, says that's the wrong way to think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以挑战方的律师杰森·默里说，那是错误的思考方式。

sentences.en: That states have authority to run presidential elections.
sentences.zh: 各州有权管理总统选举。

sentences.en: It's not located in the 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 它不在第14修正案中。

sentences.en: It's located in Article 2 of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 它位于宪法第二条中。

sentences.en: Article 2 gives states this broad power to determine how their electors are selected,
sentences.zh: 第二条赋予各州决定如何选出其选举人的广泛权力，

sentences.en: and that broad power implies the narrower power to enforce federal constitutional qualifications.
sentences.zh: 而那种广泛的权力暗示了执行联邦宪法资格要求的较窄权力。

sentences.en: Well, but the narrower power...
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是那种较窄的权力……

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: So what do you do with the, what would seem to me to be plain consequences of your position?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何处理你所持立场显而易见的后果呢？

sentences.en: Roberts picks up on another aspect of the question.
sentences.zh: 罗伯茨抓住了问题的另一个方面。

sentences.en: If Colorado's position is upheld, surely there will be disqualification proceedings on the other side, and some of those will succeed.
sentences.zh: 如果科罗拉多州的立场得到支持，肯定会有另一方的取消资格程序，其中一些会成功。

sentences.en: Saying it could result in kind of the Wild West of voting,
sentences.zh: 说这可能会导致投票方面的“狂野西部”局面，

sentences.en: where different states would not only use different standards to decide whether Donald Trump was on or off of their ballot,
sentences.zh: 不同的州不仅会使用不同的标准来决定唐纳德·特朗普是否在他们的选票上，

sentences.en: but perhaps knock President Biden off the ballot for supposed insurrectionary crimes of his own.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能因为拜登总统自己的所谓叛乱罪行而将他踢出选票。

sentences.en: I would expect that, you know, a goodly number of states will say, whoever the Democratic candidate is, you're off the ballot,
sentences.zh: 我预计，你知道，相当多的州会说，无论民主党候选人是谁，你都被踢出选票，

sentences.en: and others, for the Republican candidate, you're off the ballot, and it'll come down to just a handful of states that are going to decide the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 而其他州则会针对共和党候选人说，你被踢出选票，最终将由少数几个州来决定总统选举。

sentences.en: That's a pretty daunting consequence.
sentences.zh: 那是一个相当令人望而生畏的后果。

sentences.en: Well, certainly, Your Honor...
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，法官阁下……

sentences.en: And having this kind of back-and-forth mayhem would be a recipe for disaster in a democracy.
sentences.zh: 而且这种来回的混乱将是民主制度中的灾难根源。

sentences.en: Justice Kagan?
sentences.zh: 卡根大法官？

sentences.en: Mr. Mary, you talked, you relied on the state's extensive powers under the electors...
sentences.zh: 默里先生，你谈到，你依赖于各州在选举人方面的广泛权力……

sentences.en: And then even Justice Kagan says, listen...
sentences.zh: 然后连卡根大法官也说，听着……

sentences.en: Listen, like, what's a state doing deciding who gets to, who other citizens get to vote for for president?
sentences.zh: 听着，一个州决定其他公民可以投票给谁当总统是在做什么？

sentences.en: The practical effect of allowing Colorado to bar Trump from the ballot affects voters in other states.
sentences.zh: 允许科罗拉多州禁止特朗普出现在选票上的实际效果会影响其他州的选民。

sentences.en: Colorado is not deciding who other states get to vote for for president.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州并不是在决定其他州可以投票给谁当总统。

sentences.en: It's deciding how to assign its own electors under its Article II power.
sentences.zh: 它是在决定如何根据其第二条权力分配自己的选举人。

sentences.en: And the Constitution grants them that broad power...
sentences.zh: 而宪法授予了他们那种广泛的权力……

sentences.en: Well, but the effect of that is obvious, yes?
sentences.zh: 嗯，但其影响是显而易见的，对吧？

sentences.en: No, Your Honor, because different states can have...
sentences.zh: 不，法官阁下，因为不同的州可以有……

sentences.en: Adam, what do we think Kagan's specific fear is when she argues that letting Colorado take Trump off the ballot
sentences.zh: 亚当，我们认为卡根的具体担忧是什么？当她辩称让科罗拉多州将特朗普踢出选票

sentences.en: will affect other people's voting, she seems to be saying, outside of Colorado?
sentences.zh: 会影响科罗拉多州以外其他人的投票时，她似乎是在这么说？

sentences.en: I guess it could mean one of two things, or maybe more things.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能意味着两件事之一，或者更多的事情。

sentences.en: It could mean that it just affects the balance of power across the Electoral College.
sentences.zh: 它可能意味着这只会影响选举人团的权力平衡。

sentences.en: And makes it less likely that the candidate that someone in Texas or New Jersey wants to support is going to win because the Colorado votes drop out.
sentences.zh: 并使得德克萨斯州或新泽西州某人想要支持的候选人获胜的可能性降低，因为科罗拉多州的选票退出了。

sentences.en: It may also mean that if Colorado knocks Trump off the ballot, other states will feel persuaded that they should do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这也可能意味着，如果科罗拉多州将特朗普踢出选票，其他州会感到被说服，认为他们也应该做同样的事情。

sentences.en: That said, the lawyer for the voters, Jason Murray, doesn't get it.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，选民的律师杰森·默里并不理解这一点。

sentences.en: He says Colorado is not deciding who other states get to vote for for president.
sentences.zh: 他说科罗拉多州并不是在决定其他州可以投票给谁当总统。

sentences.en: It's deciding how to assign its own electors in the Electoral College.
sentences.zh: 它是在决定如何在选举人团中分配自己的选举人。

sentences.en: And that's just a function of states' power to enforce, to preserve their own electors and avoid disenfranchisement of their own citizens.
sentences.zh: 这只是各州行使权力以维护其自身选举人并避免其自身公民被剥夺选举权的一种功能。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And then, what about the idea that we should think about democracy, think about the right of the people to elect candidates of their choice?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于我们应该考虑民主，考虑人民选举他们选择的候选人的权利的想法呢？

sentences.en: Justice Kavanaugh also raises his own concerns about disenfranchisement.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺大法官也提出了他自己关于剥夺选举权的担忧。

sentences.en: Does that come in when we think about should we read Section 3 this way or read it that way?
sentences.zh: 当我们考虑应该这样解读第3条还是那样解读第3条时，这会涉及进来吗？

sentences.en: What about the background principle, if you agree, of democracy?
sentences.zh: 如果你们同意的话，关于民主的背景原则又如何呢？

sentences.en: I'd like to make three points on that, Justice Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我想提出三点，卡瓦诺大法官。

sentences.en: The first is that constitutional safeguards are for the purpose of safeguarding our democracy, not juSt...
sentences.zh: 第一点是，宪法保障的目的是为了保障我们的民主，而不是仅仅……

sentences.en: Jason Murray responds that Section 3 is designed to protect democracy.
sentences.zh: 杰森·默里回应说，第3条旨在保护民主。

sentences.en: This case illustrates the danger of refusing to apply Section 3 as written because the reason we're here is that President Trump tried to disenfranchise 80 million Americans who voted against him.
sentences.zh: 这个案件说明了拒绝按字面意思应用第3条的危险，因为我们之所以在这里，是因为特朗普总统试图剥夺8000万投票反对他的美国人的选举权。

sentences.en: And the Constitution doesn't require that he be given another chance.
sentences.zh: 而宪法并不要求给他第二次机会。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So, you had Murray trying very hard to convince them otherwise.
sentences.zh: 所以，默里非常努力地试图说服他们接受相反的观点。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, both Justice Kavanaugh, a conservative, and Justice Kagan, a liberal,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，保守派的卡瓦诺大法官和自由派的卡根大法官，

sentences.en: seem to be worried about the potential that a ruling that would knock Donald Trump off the ballot would amount to a kind of disenfranchisement.
sentences.zh: 似乎都对一项将唐纳德·特朗普踢出选票的裁决可能等同于一种剥夺选举权的担忧感到不安。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when we start to do the math here,
sentences.zh: 当我们开始在这里进行计算时，

sentences.en: it's not just Justice Jackson anymore who is surprising us as a liberal justice skeptical of Colorado's argument for keeping Trump off the ballot.
sentences.zh: 不再仅仅是杰克逊大法官作为一名对科罗拉多州关于将特朗普排除在选票之外的论点持怀疑态度的自由派大法官而让我们感到惊讶了。

sentences.en: We now have at least two of the liberal justices saying this might not hold up.
sentences.zh: 我们现在至少有两位自由派大法官表示这可能站不住脚。

sentences.en: As the argument goes forward, it seems that there are probably eight justices prepared to keep Trump on the ballot, and the only wild card, and it could end up being unanimous,
sentences.zh: 随着辩论的进行，似乎可能有八位大法官准备让特朗普留在选票上，唯一的变数，而且最终可能会是一致通过，

sentences.en: but the only wild card is Justice Sotomayor.
sentences.zh: 但唯一的变数是索托马约尔大法官。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Adam, if eight justices agree that Trump should be allowed to be on the ballot in Colorado, that would be kind of staggering given the nature of this case.
sentences.zh: 亚当，如果八位大法官都同意特朗普应该获准参加科罗拉多州的初选，考虑到此案的性质，这会让人相当震惊。

sentences.en: It would also be kind of staggering given the nature of this court.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这家法院的性质，这也会让人相当震惊。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is a court that has been battered, and questions have been raised about its legitimacy and authority and prestige.
sentences.zh: 这家法院一直饱受打击，人们对其合法性、权威性和声望也提出了质疑。

sentences.en: And I think the justices might view this as an opportunity to rebuild, to come together, to find consensus, and particularly in an issue where a contrary ruling,
sentences.zh: 我认为大法官们可能会将此视为一个重建、团结、寻求共识的机会，特别是在这样一个问题上：如果做出相反的裁决，

sentences.en: one that would knock a leading presidential candidate off the ballot, would give rise to a very tough reaction from half the country.
sentences.zh: 即把一位领先的总统候选人踢出选票，将会引起全国半数民众的强烈反弹。

sentences.en: Adam, it's possible, of course, that what you're saying is right, but the justices have done a kind of political analysis here and decided they want to be on the same page,
sentences.zh: 亚当，当然，你说的可能是对的，但大法官们在这里进行了一种政治分析，并决定他们想要达成共识，

sentences.en: and that page is to let voters have choice, keep Trump on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 而这个共识就是让选民有选择权，让特朗普留在选票上。

sentences.en: But is it also possible that at the end of the day,
sentences.zh: 但有没有可能，归根结底，

sentences.en: what many people saw as a strong legal case being presented by the Colorado voters and their lawyer just turned out to be weaker once it got to the highest court in front of the nation's preeminent jurists and started to kind of crumble?
sentences.zh: 许多人眼中科罗拉多州选民及其律师提出的强有力的法律论据，一旦到了最高法院，在全国最杰出的法学家面前，就开始变得站不住脚了呢？

sentences.en: Most legal scholars think that the case against Donald Trump is very strong.
sentences.zh: 大多数法律学者认为针对唐纳德·特朗普的诉讼理由非常充分。

sentences.en: The court, for various reasons, good faith legal ones, political calculations, concerns about the consequences of a ruling, were always likely to be looking for an exit ramp.
sentences.zh: 出于各种原因——无论是出于善意的法律考量、政治算计，还是对裁决后果的担忧——法院一直很可能在寻找一个下台阶。

sentences.en: It looks like they've found one and that that exit ramp will be embraced by a substantial majority, maybe even all of the justices.
sentences.zh: 看起来他们已经找到了，而且这个下台阶将得到绝大多数，甚至可能全体大法官的支持。

sentences.en: But that doesn't undermine the purely theoretical question of does Section 3 apply to Donald Trump's conduct.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能削弱一个纯粹的理论问题，即宪法第3条是否适用于唐纳德·特朗普的行为。

sentences.en: It is a reflection of kind of a judicial reality of a court that has been under some substantial stress,
sentences.zh: 这反映了一种司法现实，即这家法院一直承受着巨大的压力，

sentences.en: not wanting to use what political capital it has left on this particular cause.
sentences.zh: 不想把仅存的政治资本用在这个特定的案件上。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, for those who see what Trump did on January 6th as disqualifying for the presidency, the Colorado effort to keep him off the ballot was very meaningful, and it was,
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于那些认为特朗普在1月6日的所作所为让他失去总统竞选资格的人来说，科罗拉多州阻止他参选的努力非常有意义，而且，

sentences.en: in many of their eyes, justifiable.
sentences.zh: 在他们许多人看来，这是正当的。

sentences.en: And if the Supreme Court rules that Trump can't be held off the ballot,
sentences.zh: 如果最高法院裁定不能阻止特朗普参选，

sentences.en: it will have eliminated a major route by which American voters can hold Trump accountable for trying to overturn the results of a free and fair election.
sentences.zh: 那么它就消除了一条美国选民可以追究特朗普试图推翻自由公正选举结果责任的主要途径。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't want to undersell that point at all.
sentences.zh: 是的，我一点也不想低估这一点。

sentences.en: If the court rules as I expect it to, it will be a stinging loss for opponents of Donald Trump who saw what happened on January 6th,
sentences.zh: 如果法院如我预期的那样裁决，这对唐纳德·特朗普的反对者来说将是一个沉重的打击，他们目睹了1月6日发生的事情，

sentences.en: who consider it a vile insurrection that he incited.
sentences.zh: 并认为这是一场他煽动的卑劣叛乱。

sentences.en: And in the face of a constitutional provision that it is child's play to read as applying to him.
sentences.zh: 而且面对一条宪法条款，将其解读为适用于他简直是小儿科。

sentences.en: All of that is true.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是事实。

sentences.en: But of course, this isn't the only Trump case.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这并不是唯一针对特朗普的案件。

sentences.en: Trump is the subject of numerous criminal prosecutions, including most notably a federal case arising from some of these same events.
sentences.zh: 特朗普是多项刑事诉讼的对象，其中最引人注目的是由这些事件引发的联邦案件。

sentences.en: And that case will soon be at the Supreme Court, probably next week,
sentences.zh: 该案很快就会上诉到最高法院，可能就在下周，

sentences.en: in the form of a request from Donald Trump that he be deemed absolutely immune from criminal prosecution for his activities in trying to subvert the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 形式是唐纳德·特朗普请求法院认定他在试图颠覆2020年选举的活动中享有刑事起诉的绝对豁免权。

sentences.en: And it would not surprise me at all, Michael, if these cases would be decided in tandem and in different ways with a ruling that Trump is eligible to run,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，如果这些案件能同时审理并以不同的方式做出裁决，我一点也不会感到惊讶，即裁定特朗普有资格参选，

sentences.en: but a ruling that he is not immune from prosecution and sending the case back down for trial.
sentences.zh: 但同时裁定他不能免于起诉，并将案件发回重审。

sentences.en: Even as the election season heats up, and that would give the court the opportunity to look even-handed, to give Trump a significant victory and a significant loss,
sentences.zh: 即使在大选季升温之际，这也会给法院一个表现得公正的机会，既给了特朗普一场重大的胜利，也给了他一场重大的失败，

sentences.en: and leave it not only to the political process,
sentences.zh: 并将其留给政治程序，

sentences.en: but the ordinary criminal judicial process to decide whether Donald Trump can be held accountable for his January 6th-related activities.
sentences.zh: 以及普通的刑事司法程序来决定唐纳德·特朗普是否应该为他与1月6日相关的活动负责。

sentences.en: Well, Adam, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚当，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是薇娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天负责制作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: The special counsel investigating President Biden's handling of classified materials will not seek to prosecute him,
sentences.zh: 调查拜登总统处理机密文件不当的特别检察官将不会寻求起诉他，

sentences.en: but said there was evidence that Biden willfully retained and disclosed some sensitive material.
sentences.zh: 但表示有证据表明拜登故意保留并披露了一些敏感材料。

sentences.en: In a report released on Thursday, the special counsel said that when Biden left the White House after his vice presidency in 2017,
sentences.zh: 在周四发布的一份报告中，特别检察官表示，当拜登在2017年副总统任期结束后离开白宫时，

sentences.en: he took classified documents about Afghanistan and notebooks with handwritten entries that referred to sensitive intelligence.
sentences.zh: 他带走了关于阿富汗的机密文件，以及记录了敏感情报的手写笔记本。

sentences.en: But in an unflattering assessment, the special counsel, Robert Herr, said that a jury would be unlikely to find Biden guilty of a crime because of his poor memory.
sentences.zh: 但在一段并不光彩的评估中，特别检察官罗伯特·赫尔表示，由于拜登记忆力不佳，陪审团不太可能判定他有罪。

sentences.en: Her said that Biden could not remember key dates, such as when his vice presidency ended and when his eldest son, Beau, had died.
sentences.zh: 赫尔说，拜登记不住关键日期，比如他的副总统任期何时结束，以及他的长子博何时去世。

sentences.en: Do you know your memory has gotten worse, Mr. President?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，你知道你的记忆力变差了吗？

sentences.en: My memory is not.
sentences.zh: 我的记忆力没有。

sentences.en: My memory is fine.
sentences.zh: 我的记忆力很好。

sentences.en: During a news conference a few hours later, Biden angrily rejected the claim that his memory was in decline.
sentences.zh: 几个小时后的新闻发布会上，拜登愤怒地驳斥了关于他记忆力衰退的说法。

sentences.en: Take a look at what I've done since I've become president.
sentences.zh: 看看我成为总统以来所做的一切。

sentences.en: None of you thought I could pass any of the things I got passed.
sentences.zh: 你们谁也没想到我能通过我所通过的那些法案。

sentences.en: How'd that happen?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: You know, I guess I just forgot what was going on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我猜我只是忘了当时发生了什么。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Lindsay Garrison, and Mary Wilson, with help from Alexandra Lee Young.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗伯·齐普科、琳赛·加里森和玛丽·威尔逊制作，亚历山德拉·李·杨提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett and Brendan Klinkenberg, contains original music by Marian Lozano and Corey Shreppel, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 节目由佩奇·考维特和布伦丹·克林肯伯格编辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺和科里·施雷佩尔的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方收听。
